title: Enhance interactive dog-blog components: like toggle, email validation, a11y labels
body:
## Goal
The three client-side components (LikeButton, CommentBox, NewsletterSignup) in `moonexpr/dog-blog-demo` already render interactively with basic `useState` — but each has a stub gap to close.

## Research findings
- Stack: Next.js 14, React 18, TypeScript, Tailwind. No form library, no state management beyond bare `useState`. All three already have `"use client"`.
- LikeButton (`src/components/LikeButton.tsx`): increment-only; should toggle liked/unliked with `aria-pressed`; count is ephemeral per mount (no per-post persistence needed for demo); `postSlug` prop already present.
- CommentBox (`src/components/CommentBox.tsx`): add-to-list + empty guard already work; needs a visible `<label>` on the text input for accessibility.
- NewsletterSignup (`src/components/NewsletterSignup.tsx`): success state already shown; current `@`-only validation is too weak — use `type="email"` native validation plus an inline error message for invalid submissions; needs `<label>` on the email input.
- No test suite — acceptance is manual verification in the dev server.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] LikeButton toggles liked/unliked state; `aria-pressed` reflects current state; rapid repeated clicks do not race (guard with disabled state during optimistic update).
- [ ] CommentBox has a visible `<label>` (or visually-hidden equivalent) associated with its text input via `htmlFor`/`id`; existing empty-input guard is preserved.
- [ ] NewsletterSignup email input has a visible `<label>`; invalid/empty email is rejected client-side with an inline error message; valid email shows the existing success state.
- [ ] All changes are pure client-side (no backend, no DB, no fetch calls); state is ephemeral per page-load — localStorage not required.
- [ ] No new npm dependencies introduced; use only the existing React `useState` pattern.
- [ ] `npm run build` passes with no TypeScript errors.

## Scope
Edit only the three component files:
- `src/components/LikeButton.tsx`
- `src/components/CommentBox.tsx`
- `src/components/NewsletterSignup.tsx`

Do NOT change `src/app/page.tsx` or any other file unless a build error demands it.

## Verification
Run `npm run dev`, open the app in a browser, and manually verify:
1. Clicking the like button toggles it; `aria-pressed` reflects state in DevTools.
2. Submitting a blank comment does nothing; a non-blank comment appends to the list.
3. Submitting blank/invalid email shows inline error; valid email shows the success state.
4. `npm run build` exits 0.
